title: The notice period on the target: no period length, no timer home, no timer-ledger write path, no published operation of the four consumed services, no notice-period state value and no service event
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-003); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md; _work/msr/context/S4.md
description: Missing: the length of the statutory notice period, which R-LIT-07 gives only as the words notice period by product and type. Missing: the warning threshold of R-UNI-31 behind MSG-S4-002. Conflict: the FSD S4 A2.2 says the proof of delivery is written onto the notice, while the Ownership Map gives S4 only hearing and legal_action, so the notice row and its served result belong to rwb-comms and cannot be written here. Conflict: FSD S4 A2.3.2 names a Quartz scheduler and the legacy data block names a timer table, while the ownership rows give S4 no timer table and the case service holds the timers, so the period has no row to live in. Missing: the operation names and the field lists of the notice read and unserved announcement of rwb-comms, of the proof attach of rwb-document, of the case read and route fact of rwb-case and of the approval route of rwb-decision, none of which is in this story's dependency rows. Missing: any value of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS that names a notice period, a served or an unserved notice, since the list holds OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED and WITHDRAWN. Missing: the event set, since the ownership rows give S4 zero events while Architecture v5 slide 19 shows NoticeDelivered as an input of the service. Missing: the business text of the 409 of a notice that is not NOTICE_DISPATCHED.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.3.3.1 gives VR-S4-003-1, R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-15 and BR-S4-003 and no period value; A2.3.2 gives the integration points Workbench and Quartz scheduler and the prerequisite FEAT-CWC-11. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-LIT-07 the timing column notice period by product and type, R-LIT-08 the timing 7 days, R-LIT-15 the timing 3 working days with owner Workbench, and R-UNI-31 a warning threshold it does not state. TSD S4 T3.1 defines legal_action and hearing only, T3.2 gives the two lists of six values each, T4 gives 79 rules over 38 states, T5.3 gives Events None and T5.1 gives INT-09 and INT-33. The legacy story RWB-E5-003 lists recovery_case, timer DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036, v_ace_customer DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074, notice DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, decision_log_entry and rule_row in its data block and two endpoints, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions and POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve. The context pack gives S4 two tables, five operations, zero events, zero jobs and one workflow, and Architecture v5 slide 10 gives the case service the timers and the notices to rwb-comms.
proposed: Carry the legacy sentences unchanged with their origin tags and record the target reading: the period starts at delivered_at and its length is a versioned reference row by product group and notice type, whose value waits for the business; the period is a durable timer of the LitigationWorkflow stage on queue rwb-litigation and the timer ledger DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 is rwb-case's, so no timer table exists in rwb_litigation; the notice and its served result are rwb-comms's and are read and announced on its contract; the proof is attached through rwb-document; the three case states are announced as route facts to rwb-case; the approval at right A routes through rwb-decision; no Kafka event is published or consumed and the delivery result is a workflow signal; the 409 is published with its causes and its messageId slot while its text waits for the C1 message catalogue.

title: The notice-period contract: no period element behind a column, no index set, no operation name for the four consumed services, no notice table of this service and no text for the 409 or the 400
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-003); _work/msr/context/S4.md
description: Missing: the index set of legal_action beyond the primary key on id, which no source read for this key declares. Missing: any source value for the notice period length, the proof window instant and the warning window, all of which the document must name as references and cannot fix. Conflict: no column of TSD S4 T3.1 can hold the period start or expiry, so the period has to be declared as a workflow element and not as a schema element. Missing: the operation names and answer field lists of the notice read and unserved announcement of rwb-comms, the proof attach of rwb-document, the case route fact of rwb-case and the approval route of rwb-decision. Conflict: the FSD S4 A2.2 writes the delivery confirmation onto the notice while the Ownership Map gives S4 no notice table, so the contract publishes the approve operation and declares the notice as a consumed shape only. Missing: the business text of the 409 and the code of the 400, since the TSD error sets name statuses and the message catalogue names no message for either.
evidence: TSD S4 T-A.1 gives five operations and their rights, idempotency and no 400 status; T-A.2 names the request and response entities and lists 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; T3.1 gives DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 with no period or delivered_at field; T3.2 gives the two lists; T4 gives the rule table. FSD S4 A2.2 writes the delivery confirmation onto the notice and A2.3 gives the three rules of this key. The legacy story RWB-E5-003 names MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-S4-001 and MSG-S4-002 and no 409 text. The context pack ownership rows give S4 the tables hearing and legal_action, five operations on base /api/recovery/litigation/v1, zero events, zero jobs and the workflow LitigationWorkflow, and Architecture v5 slide 10 gives notices to rwb-comms.
proposed: Publish the resource as TSD S4 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T3.1 state it and nothing more: the three operations on base /api/recovery/litigation/v1, the LegalActionRequest, LegalAction and NoticeActionUpdate schemas over DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, the legal_action DDL template with the T3.0 standard columns and the primary key only, the six error statuses with the problem envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule on the two writes, the versioning rule and the fakes; the period is declared once as an element of the noticeDeliveryResult signal and of the read answer, the notice is declared as a consumed shape of rwb-comms, and the four consumed operation names and the 409 text carry this row.
